subject: Re: GCP Marketplace private offer — tiered drawdown roadmap for Avalon
messages:
From: Jesse Park <jesse.park@avalon.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GCP private offer: drawdown structure question

Hi Priyom / Laura,

Thanks again for the intro call earlier. Procurement at Avalon wants to understand how Redwood recommends structuring the private-offer drawdown for our initial commit. A few constraints from our side:

- We expect three primary SKUs (inference, embeddings, and batch-ingest) with uneven consumption profiles.
- Procurement prefers quarterly drawdowns aligned to invoicing to match their internal finance cadence.
- They want a plan that avoids large front-loading but still gives us co-sell incentives on GCP.

I've attached our Q3–Q4 demand forecast (Avalon_Demand_Forecast.xlsx). Can you share an example cadence you typically recommend (percent by quarter and fallback rules)? Also curious about how co-sell eligibility maps to front-loaded redemption vs steady burn.

Would be great to have a short template roadmap we can present to our CFO next week.

Thanks,
Jesse Park
Head of Cloud Ops, Avalon AI
jesse.park@avalon.ai
Attachment: Avalon_Demand_Forecast.xlsx (xlsx)

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Jesse Park <jesse.park@avalon.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GCP private offer: drawdown structure question

Jesse — thanks for sending the forecast, this is helpful. Quick reply with a recommended path and a few open items.

Summary recommendation (high-level):
- Tiered drawdown model: 20% initial unlock at activation -> 30% spread over Q1 -> remaining 50% evenly across next three quarters.
- Quarterly invoicing alignment: we can map drawdown events to your invoice dates so consumption credits hit the same period. That satisfies most procurement teams.
- Co-sell gating: to qualify for co-sell, GCP typically looks at committed churn reduction and activation metrics (we can help shepherd the paperwork with the partner team). Front-loading up to 30% increases co-sell momentum but is negotiable.

Open items we need from you to finalize:
1) SKU-level monthly forecast (so we can model token parity and estimated burn).
2) Preferred invoice dates and billing contact.
3) Any hard constraints on unused-credit expiry or carry-forward.

I've attached a slightly edited T&Cs PDF with our suggested drawdown clauses for private offers (Private_Offer_T&Cs_v3.pdf) and a quick model prototype. Marissa/Ben — tagging you for ops feasibility and to propose a canary SKU release plan.

Next step: 30-min sync early next week to lock cadence and trigger DocuSign. Available slots: Mon 4/26 10:00–11:30 PT, Tue 4/27 14:00–16:00 PT.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
Attachment: Private_Offer_T&Cs_v3.pdf (pdf)

Priyom — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from procurement after they reviewed your notes:

- Quarterly invoicing is a must. They need a firm drawdown date that ties to each quarter's invoice, not just a mapping.
- They want a 12-month total commitment but with the ability to reallocate unused credits between the three SKUs within the year.
- Avalon prefers the initial unlock to be 15% rather than 20% to avoid aggressive front-loading in the first billing cycle.

I've uploaded a trimmed forecast with SKU breakout: Avalon_Demand_Forecast_v2.xlsx (same attachment name for ease). Can you model the recommended percentages against that sheet and return a simple one-page cadence table we can present to finance? Also please confirm whether granting 15% up-front would materially affect co-sell eligibility.

Thanks — will aim to get our billing lead on the call if we lock a slot.

Jesse

Subject: Re: GCP private offer: drawdown structure question — ops and co-sell notes

Folks — quick ops perspective and co-sell play: 

- 15% initial unlock is fine from an operational standpoint; it reduces risk on our side and still gives Avalon runway to demonstrate early usage.
- To preserve co-sell momentum without heavy front-load, propose we require a 45-day activation window after PO issuance where Avalon must onboard at least one customer on the inference SKU (can be a canary customer). If activation criteria met, an early-release tranche of +10% is triggered.
- For invoicing alignment, we charge at invoice generation but can surface reconciliations in the following billing period — works for most finance teams.

Next steps:
1) Priyom — create the one-page cadence table modeling 15% initial + conditional + even spread thereafter and share with Jesse.
2) Ben — please prepare a canary SKU rollout checklist (permits, quotas, monitoring hooks).
3) Laura — loop in marketplace onboarding to start partner listing review when legal signs.

I'll intro Michael L. from GCP on the next thread to coordinate co-sell paperwork and timelines.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success & Co-sell Enablement, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

- Remainder: 75% evenly distributed across the remaining quotas billed quarterly over the next 10 months.
